---
title: Read a view
description: Read the items a saved view lists from the server, or its items and groups from a device's working copy.
---

A [view](/catalog/view) saves which items to list, in what order and how they group. **Read it from the server** for a page of its items, or **read it offline** from a device's [working copy](/build/working-copies), which also counts its groups.

The examples read the "Tasks by priority" view that [Save a list as a view](/build/save-a-view) creates, with a credential that can read `system.view` and `core.task`. In the TypeScript example, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows.

## Read a view's items from the server

Ask for a page of the items the view lists:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa views items <view-id> --limit 50
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /views/<view-id>/items?limit=50
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/views/{id}/items", {
  params: { path: { id: viewId }, query: { limit: 50 } },
});
```

The answer holds `data`, the items in the view's order, and `next_cursor`. Send the cursor back as `cursor` for the next page, and **stop only when it's `null`**: a page can be short, or empty, with more to follow. The CLI's `--all` follows it for you. A page holds 50 items unless you ask for 1 to 200.

What the server lists:

- **Only what the credential can read.** A view never widens access: an item of a type the credential can't read is left out, and so is anything reached through it.
- **No system items.**
- **The view's order.** Sort keys apply in turn, first key first. An item missing a sorted field comes after every item that holds it, in either direction, so the tasks with no due date come last. Items that tie on every key go by ascending ID, or in the key's direction when the view sorts by one timestamp alone. A view with no sort lists the newest `occurred_at` first, and ties there go by descending ID.
- **Under `beneath`, the item and everything under it** by `parent-of`, at any depth, each once, and nothing in the bin.
- **No groups.** The server lists the items in order and leaves grouping to the app or the working copy.

A read is refused with:

- `400 validation_error` for a `limit` out of range, or a cursor from another view or an earlier version of this one. Start again without the cursor.
- `400 invalid_transition` for a view revoked when the item it sat under was deleted.
- `403 type_not_permitted` when the credential reads no type.
- `403 edge_type_not_permitted` when the view names `beneath` and the credential can't read `parent-of` edges.
- `404 item_not_found` when no view the credential can read has the ID, which includes a credential with no read on `system.view`.

## Read a view from a working copy

A device's working copy answers a view with no connection, sorting and grouping the items it holds the way the server would. It can't sort by `last_activity_at`, because it doesn't hold when an item's rows last changed: a view sorted by it is refused as `invalid`.

### Fill the working copy

While connected, hydrate the view type and every type the view's query needs:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device --db ./copy.sqlite hydrate --type system.view --type core.task --tier all
```

```text
hydrated 5 item(s) and 0 edge(s) of system.view,core.task at all in 2 page(s); cursor 46
```

</Terminal>

**Hold the whole query**, including its tier: a view over both tiers needs `--tier all`. A group by `edge[<type>]` or `backref[<type>]`, or a filter with a `backref` condition, needs that edge type held whole, so add `--edge-type <type>`. A view with `beneath` needs `parent-of` held whole too. Hydration needs the server and a credential, as [Connect to a server](/reference/cli#connect-to-a-server) describes; the reads below need neither.

### Read the items

List the views the copy holds, then read one view's items in its order:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device --db ./copy.sqlite views list
marfa device --db ./copy.sqlite items list --view <view-id> --limit 50
```

```text
01a1f18b-6a06-74fc-b94d-1b25f2795b17 active at version 1: Tasks by priority
01a1f18a-8a77-7343-be83-568c1358ddf4  core.task  2026-11-19T02:02:30.903Z  Renew the passport
01a1f18a-8a51-7273-862a-fab8df0370ac  core.task  2026-11-19T02:02:30.865Z  Service the boiler
01a1f18a-8a66-7087-9723-55c045cc6b40  core.task  2026-11-19T02:02:30.886Z  Fix the garden gate
01a1f18a-8a87-7556-ac04-ce01c159cc61  core.task  2026-11-19T02:02:30.919Z  Clear the gutters
```

</Terminal>

A copy pages by `--offset`. With `--json`, each read answers `data`, `next_cursor` and `completeness`. To search within the view's query, pass the view to search, which orders matches by relevance:

```bash
marfa device --db ./copy.sqlite search "boiler" --view <view-id>
```

### Read the groups

A view with a `group` answers one count for each group. A view with no `group` answers one group, counting every item it lists.

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device --db ./copy.sqlite views groups <view-id>
```

```text
"high": 1 item(s)
"low": 1 item(s)
"medium": 1 item(s)
"urgent": 1 item(s)
```

</Terminal>

With `--json`, the groups are entries in `data`, each with a `key` and a `count`. **An item counts once in each group it belongs to**: a task with two tags belongs to both tag groups, so the counts can add up to more than the items. An item missing the field belongs to the `null` group. An edge group's key is the ID at the other end of the edge.

The view's `group.order` puts the groups it names first, and `group.hidden` leaves the groups it names out. The others follow in value order, with `null` last.

A date group follows the view's `group.bucket`. Its key is the first date of the bucket as `YYYY-MM-DD`, and weeks start on Monday. Buckets follow the calendar in the device's time zone, or in the one you name:

```bash
marfa device --db ./copy.sqlite views groups <view-id> --time-zone Europe/London
```

### Read a view in an app

An app on the Swift SDK reads a view from its working copy with the same calls as any other read:

```swift
let page = try await copy.items.list(inView: viewID, limit: 50)
let groups = try await copy.items.groups(inView: viewID, timeZone: .current)
```

`copy.items.views()` lists the views the copy holds, and `copy.search(_:inView:limit:)` searches within one. The Swift SDK also writes views and follows one as it changes: [Views and folders](/reference/swift-sdk/items#saved-views) shows both.

### When the copy can't answer

**A view's items, groups and search are never answered in part.** If the copy can't answer the whole query or grouping, the read is refused with the reason, such as:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device --db ./copy.sqlite items list --view <view-id>
```

```text
marfa: this copy cannot answer the view's query: the view holds core.bookmark, and this copy's slice does not take them; hydrate with them
```

</Terminal>

The same happens while a hydration is unfinished, when the copy is stale because the instance's event log let its cursor go, and when an edge type a group or `backref` condition needs isn't held whole. In Swift, the read throws `MarfaError.invalid` with the reason, or `MarfaError.hydrationIncomplete`. When connected, hydrate what the view needs and read again. A field that no item holds is not a refusal: it sorts as missing and groups under `null`.

The rules are in the contract's [views](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/views.md#reading-what-a-view-lists) chapter and the [views read from a copy](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/device.md#views-read-from-a-copy) section of its device chapter.
